title: Crispy Garlic Pork
seoTitle: Italian Sausage and Veg Sheet Pan | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Sweet Italian sausage with roasted peppers, onion, and zucchini
subtitle: Sweet Italian sausage with roasted peppers, onion, and zucchini
description: Sweet Italian sausage links roast with bell peppers, red onion, and zucchini until caramelized and ready for hoagie rolls or straight tray service.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crispy Garlic Pork in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat oven and toss ingredients
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss sausage, peppers, onion, zucchini, tomatoes, garlic, oil, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.

steps.title: Spread on sheet pans
steps.instruction: Divide between two half-sheets in a single layer with sausage pieces spaced for airflow and veg in gaps between meat. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Roast until sausage is done
steps.instruction: Roast 24–28 minutes, stirring once halfway, until sausage reads 165°F and pepper edges char lightly with softened centers. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and check texture
steps.instruction: Rest 3 minutes. Sausage should snap when bitten with juicy interior; vegetables tender with slight char, not mushy. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Serve on rolls or tray
steps.instruction: Pile onto hoagie rolls with provolone or serve straight from tray with crusty bread for soaking pan juices. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Hot Italian sausage swap adds heat—offer separately for mixed crews.
Provolone under broiler 2 minutes makes instant sausage subs.
Line pans with foil for faster cleanup of rendered sausage fat.
leftovers: Sausage and veg over polenta next day.
Chop into a pasta skillet with olive oil and parmesan.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Minimal prep, maximum flavor. Familiar Italian combo that feels like a sub shop without leaving the hall.
mealPrepNotes: Slice sausage links into 2-inch pieces for faster cooking. Cut veg uniform for even roast. Station: Use two half-sheets so sausage browns instead of steaming in released fat. Station: Rotate pans halfway for even caramelization in a crowded oven. Station: Offer hoagie rolls at the line for sausage-and-pepper subs.
